title: Orbital motion: why do planets change speed?
subtitle: 13 steps of Kepler's Laws (26 in the full investigation)
body:
Step 1 of 13 read

Three questions about an orbit

What path does a planet follow around its star, and what sets how fast it moves and how long its year is? You will answer it in the live orbit view: predict first, then measure distances, speeds and years in orbits you choose.

Johannes Kepler answered it four hundred years ago from positions of Mars measured without a telescope. Why he trusted them comes after your first prediction.

💡 While an investigation is running, clicking selects an object without opening the inspector card, and placing new objects is switched off so a stray click cannot alter the system you are measuring.

Where Kepler's version breaks

Newton's correction replaces Kepler's constant with one that depends on M + m rather than M alone.
